key_insight: The paper reports the first synthesis of anhydrous cubic Na2IrCl6 single crystals, completing the vacancy-ordered A2IrCl6 family and identifying it as a new candidate for a Jeff = 1/2 magnetic ground state.
engineering_relevance: This establishes a structurally well-defined iridate platform for studying how crystal symmetry, spin-orbit coupling, and competing exchange interactions shape magnetic behavior in vacancy-ordered double perovskites.
method: Used thermogravimetric analysis to confirm the absence of lattice water and assess thermal stability.
Performed structural and magnetic characterization to verify fcc symmetry and antiferromagnetic ordering.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an antiferromagnetic transition temperature of 1.91 K and thermal stability up to 453 K, supporting the material’s cubic anhydrous phase.
watch_item: The magnetic ground state is still a candidate interpretation, so further spectroscopic and theoretical validation is needed before claiming a definitive Jeff = 1/2 state.
paper_title: Na$_2$Ir$^\text{IV}$Cl$_6$: The Missing Member of the Perfectly Cubic Vacancy Ordered $A_2$IrCl$_6$ Family, Another Potential $J_{eff}$ = $\frac{1}{2}$ Ground State Candidate
